activities.title: Turn your inventory into a 4-tab workbook
activities.intro: Use your Lab 3 inventory. Copying the sheet gives Feb and Mar the same headers and formulas as Jan.

items: Rename your inventory sheet (Sheet1 or Inventory) to Jan. Give it a colour.
Copy the Jan sheet twice: right-click, Move or Copy, tick Create a copy. In Google Sheets use Duplicate.
Rename the copies Feb and Mar.
Insert a new sheet named Summary. Drag it to the far left.

blocks.prompt: How many sheet tabs does your workbook have now?
Which tab is now at the far left?
Optional: a screenshot of your tab bar

help: Excel shows Jan (2) after copying, and Google Sheets shows Copy of Jan. That is just the default name: double-click the tab and rename it.
Summary ended up on the right? Drag its tab to the left.
In Excel, a deleted sheet cannot be brought back with Ctrl + Z. Save a copy first if you are unsure.

activities.title: Make the Summary sheet read every month
activities.intro: Link the Summary tab to each month's total in E10. Type the deck's Feb and Mar quantities first so your answers can be checked.

items: On the Feb tab, type these quantities in C2:C9: 20, 25, 8, 3, 5, 10, 6, 2.
On the Mar tab, type these quantities in C2:C9: 30, 28, 12, 5, 6, 15, 10, 4.
On the Summary tab type A1 Month, B1 Total Cost. In A2:A4 type Jan, Feb, Mar.
In B2 type =, click the Jan tab, click E10, press Enter. Do the same for Feb in B3 and Mar in B4.
In B5 type =SUM(B2:B4); in B6 type =AVERAGE(B2:B4).
Change one quantity on the Feb tab and watch the Summary change. Then change it back.

blocks.prompt: What does the Summary show for Feb (B3)?
What is the Q1 total in B5?
What is the monthly average in B6?
What formula is in B2 of the Summary?

help: Same number for all three months? Your formulas point to the same sheet. Click each cell and read the formula bar.
Do not type the ! by hand. Type =, then click the tab and the cell.
A tab name with spaces needs quotes: ='Jan 2026'!E10.
LibreOffice writes the link as =$Jan.E10. That is correct.

activities.title: Freeze, sort, filter, then put it back
activities.intro: Four quick tasks on your Jan sheet. Answer as you go, then reset the sheet at the end.

items: Freeze: freeze the top row. Scroll down to check.
Sort: select A2:E9 and sort by Total Cost, largest to smallest.
Filter: show only items with Unit Cost greater than 300.
Reset: clear the filter, then sort by Item, A to Z.

blocks.prompt: After sorting largest to smallest, which item is in row 2?
With the filter on, how many items are left?
Which items are left after the filter? Pick all that apply.
With the filter still on, what does the TOTAL in E10 show?

help: Got five items? You probably filtered Total Cost instead of Unit Cost.
The TOTAL row moved in the sort? Undo, then select A1:E9 only.
Never sort one column alone. If Excel asks, choose Expand the selection.
Clear the filter when you are done, or a co-worker will think half the data is missing.

activities.title: Quick check: renaming a linked sheet

blocks.prompt: The Summary shows =Feb!E10. A co-worker renames the Feb tab to "February". What happens?
options: You must retype every Summary formula
